senses.gloss: a first success with new customers
gloss_distractors: a formal agreement between two firms
a written plan for the year
senses.definition: Progress made into a market, account or group that was closed to you before.
senses.caution: It admits the other side still says no. It also treats them as opponents, which can sound hostile when they never resisted you.
senses.example: We've made real inroads with the risk function, but nobody there is signing anything this quarter.

cues.text: A sponsor asks how the push into the private markets business is going. Two teams out of eleven are using the platform, and you want a word that is honestly partial.
You are writing a quarterly update about a department that ignored you for a year and has finally started taking meetings.
A director asks whether the backlog of data quality issues is shrinking. It is, slowly, and you do not want to claim victory.

A fear of water shut you out of swimming for years and you have begun to get somewhere with it. A friend asks how it is going, and you want a word for early, partial progress into something that was closed to you.
A relative who has been cold with you for years has started returning calls, and you are telling a friend where things stand.

distractors: Permission given once and in advance to cover a whole class of later decisions.
The preparation done in advance of a moment where any gap would cost you dearly.
Real agreement from the people whose cooperation the work needs, not just their nods.
A rule of thumb that is quick and usually good enough.
To avoid something on principle when you could have taken it.
